title: Per-task GM metadata attention: the meta8 and meta11 ABIs
formula: out(B*MQ,128) bf16 = sum_n hif8(exp(s - m)) @ V / sum(exp(s - m)), s = Q K^T / sqrt(128) over uint8 HiFloat8 Q(B*MQ,128) and K/V(B*N,128); every task's geometry is read from an int32 GM table of 8 or 11 fields
study_for: The same idea as `attention.a5_pfa_hif8_metadata` moved one level down: the int32 GM table is per TASK rather than per core. `meta8` carries eight fields per (query tile, key tile); `meta11` adds the cache slot `sm`, the q-buffer parity `qm` and the `first_k`/`last_k` flags and drops `kt`, because the flags replace every `kt` comparison. Read the pair to see what those extra fields buy: +3 GM scalar loads per step pair against -7 in-core ALU ops.

Scalar geometry that lives in GM has to be loaded explicitly. Every field goes through `Var.GetValueFrom` on a one-element GM view (`meta[0:1, i:i+1]`), not through an implicit read — all-integer tensor indexing is not part of the GM-view syntax.

A tail correction worth copying: D-214 makes the tail PV contract to the valid V rows (`matmul(..., k=v_rows)`, and `l1v[lag][0:v_rows]`) instead of zero-filling a full L1 tile that the next iteration would overwrite anyway.

The two-owner flash-decoding merge. A core boundary that lands inside a query tile leaves two partial (max, sum, numerator) triples in the split workspace; the post-`allvec_wait` tail rescales one against the other and publishes the row. `meta8_split` and `meta8_split_tail` are the cases where that path runs at all.
do_not_copy_when: You are looking for the scaled-P V7 ABI. Both kernels here retain UNSCALED HiFloat8 probabilities, which is a different ABI from the per-core metadata unit.

You want the source's performance story. The source-era speedup hypotheses are historical context; this unit makes no speed or hardware-support claim of its own, and the meta8/meta11 pair is a comparison of ABIs, not a ranking.

You need the emitter to prove a local capacity. The staging extents here (`valid_n`, `v_rows`, `valid_m`) are run-time metadata loads, which is exactly what the PyPTO path refuses under RFC-0013 — see main.py's `pypto_pro` note before copying the shape into a kernel that has to emit there.
